quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic laws, ignoring the construction zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be careful when a sign, flagger, or police officer tells you to. Not following directions is illegal and dangerous for workers in construction zones.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, drivers should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think most children have left the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop signal on. Do not move forward until the stop arm is pulled back.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:

options.text: Go faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid hitting other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Entrance ramps have acceleration lanes for this purpose. Signal, check for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always stop completely at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: A steady yellow light at an intersection means:

options.text: Go.
Let other cars go.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, go through carefully.

questions.question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:

options.text: Is only necessary when other traffic is around.
Is a good habit and required by law.
Is only necessary during the move, not before.
Is not necessary if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving left or right. Always signal before leaving a curb.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and let it pass.
Move to the right side of the road safely and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Stay on the right side and keep moving slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road safely and stop.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, you must yield to an emergency vehicle with lights and/or siren coming from any direction. Move as far right as possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn. You should:

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to ask drivers to let you through.
Go around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can travel under dangerous conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can travel under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to travel under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can travel under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed under ideal conditions. You can drive slower, but not faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or bad weather. If road conditions make the posted speed unsafe, drive below it.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle has bright high beams and will not dim them, glance toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see enough to stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: In New Jersey, drivers under 21 are considered to be driving under the influence at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.01 percent.
0.05 percent.
0.1 percent.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 will face penalties if their BAC is 0.01 percent or higher.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol concentration.
Stops the effects of alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol concentration.
Raises your blood alcohol concentration.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol concentration.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your BAC. It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or change your BAC.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to stop for a red or yellow light.

questions.question: Which of these are used on some highways to guide drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows show which lanes to use for going straight or turning.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is dropping off children:

options.text: Do not go until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking on the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: You should use extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane because:

options.text: The person is deaf.
The person is a police officer.
The person is blind.
The person has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The person is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane signals that a pedestrian is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is breaking the law.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the legal right-of-way.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is breaking the law.
questions.explanation: Do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation. You must yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You don't need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Drivers should watch carefully for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller and harder to spot than cars. Many crashes happen because drivers did not see them. Stay alert for these smaller and less protected road users.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, you should:

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Block other cars from passing you.
Use your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, you must pull off and let cars pass you. Only drive below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?

options.text: A rectangular red sign
A circular green sign
A diamond-shaped yellow sign
A triangular orange sign

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem drive at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee
Exercise
Wait for your body to remove the alcohol naturally
Take a cold shower

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to remove the alcohol naturally
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they don't change your BAC.

questions.question: Before turning left, what must you do?

options.text: Sound your horn
Yield to oncoming vehicles
Swing to the right side of your lane
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must give the right-of-way to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line at a stop sign. The vehicles ahead have passed through and there is no cross traffic. What must you do?

options.text: You may go through without stopping again
You must stop again at the stop sign before going
You may slowly roll past the stop sign
You may follow the car ahead without stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign before going
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip your stop because other cars are moving.

questions.question: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Leave your car and walk for help
Lie down in your car and sleep
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention
Stay in your car, as rescuers will find you there

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car, as rescuers will find you there
questions.explanation: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. Rescuers are more likely to find you if you remain in your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in suburban residential areas unless posted otherwise?

options.text: 10 mph
35 mph
45 mph
65 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in suburban residential areas is 35 mph unless a different speed limit is posted. Follow posted signs if they show a different speed limit.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane
The lane closest to where you came from
Either lane
Neither lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane.

questions.question: What can a leaking exhaust system do?

options.text: Cause your engine to use too much oil
Require your vehicle to need a tune-up sooner
Make you feel sleepy while driving
Start fires along country roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel sleepy while driving
questions.explanation: An exhaust system removes toxic gases, reduces noise, and cools hot gases from the engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust system are dangerous and can make you drowsy while driving.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights at an intersection are not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your car and wait for power to return
Use hand signals to show other drivers your plans
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping
Treat it like a four-way stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers and proceed with caution when it is your turn.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane
Keep driving in your lane
Pull to the right curb and stop
Stop exactly where you are

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right curb or side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: Where is passing not allowed?

options.text: In a tunnel.
On a bridge.
In an underpass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass in an underpass, on a bridge, or in a tunnel. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass from your direction.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions can hurt your driving ability. If you are worried, angry, afraid, excited, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress reduces your concentration. Wait to drive if you are emotionally upset.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down as you approach the intersection. You must let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: When railroad crossing signals are flashing, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop your vehicle at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Also watch for lowered gates or the sound of a train.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes, pulling from a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Unnecessary.
Not needed if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is broken down.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely and without getting in the way of other traffic.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: Just the driver.
Just adult passengers.
Just child passengers.
All people in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: All people in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: The driver and all passengers must wear a seat belt. Drivers, front seat passengers, and passengers under 18 who do not wear a seat belt can be ticketed. Drivers are responsible for all passengers under 18. Back seat passengers 18 and older can also be ticketed if the vehicle was stopped for another reason.

questions.question: You may turn right on red:

options.text: When there is a sign that says no right turn on red.
Before pedestrians have finished crossing the intersection.
After you stop completely and let pedestrians and other vehicles pass.
Without stopping first.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you stop completely and let pedestrians and other vehicles pass.
questions.explanation: You can turn right on red after coming to a full stop. Only turn if it is safe and if there is no sign that says no right turn on red. Watch for pedestrians crossing in front of you.

questions.question: What should worry you most when you see this sign?

options.text: Your headlights will not work properly because one side of your car is higher.
A tire could be damaged if you drift onto the shoulder.
You could hydroplane if there is water on the shoulder.
You could lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could lose control of your vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the shoulder is lower than the road ahead. If one wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not brake hard or turn sharply. This will cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend. You should:

options.text: Not worry about it because all vehicles are the same.
Hide from your friend that you do not know the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how it works before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how it works before you drive.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes learning where the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn are located and how they work. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and road. Tires with low air pressure or bad tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:

options.text: Try to drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no train is coming and keep driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs warn drivers that a train may be nearby. Always obey these signs. Never drive around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: Orange signs are:

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are diamond-shaped, orange, and have black letters or symbols. They warn you that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Bicycle store.
Soft shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign (with the arrow below) shows where bicycles cross or ride near traffic. Drive carefully in this area because cyclists are likely present.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level higher than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level higher than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving ability will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: When changing lanes you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal to show your intention.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal so other drivers know you plan to change lanes. Look for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the narrow bridge ahead.
The bridge ahead has one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead fits only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that the bridge ahead may be too narrow to safely meet or pass a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking hard and carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic when returning to the road.
